facts.text: The collared sparrowhawk is a small, slim bird of prey that specialises in hunting small birds.
facts.quote: As its name implies the collared sparrowhawk is a specialist in hunting small birds.

facts.text: It has long legs, and the last segment of its middle toe projects beyond the claws of the other toes.
facts.quote: It is characterised by its slight brow ridges and slender feet. The last segment of their middle toe projects beyond the claws of the other toes.

facts.text: It has rounded wings, a long square tail, yellow eyes and long legs.
facts.quote: They are small, fierce, finely built with rounded wings, long square tail, yellow eyes and long legs.

facts.text: Adults are slate-grey above with a chestnut half collar and finely barred rufous and white underparts.
facts.quote: Adults have slate-grey upper parts, sometimes with a brown wash, and a chestnut half collar. The underparts are finely barred rufous and white.

facts.text: It takes prey by stealth and surprise, either hunting in flight or bursting from a concealed perch among foliage.
facts.quote: Sparrowhawks rely on stealth and surprise to catch their prey, hunting in flight or bursting from a concealed perch among foliage.

facts.text: It eats small birds, insects, lizards and even small mammals including bats.
facts.quote: They also catch insects, lizards and small mammals (including small bats).

facts.text: The nest is a platform of sticks lined with green leaves, built in the fork of a living tree.
facts.quote: The nest is a platform of sticks 27–32 cm across, 12–15 cm deep, lined with green leaves around 4–39 m above ground in the fork of a living tree.

facts.text: Females usually lay three or four eggs, and incubation takes about 35 days.
facts.quote: The clutch size is usually three or four eggs, ranging from two to five. Incubation takes 35 days, and the nesting period is about 28–33 days.

facts.text: It lives across mainland Australia, Tasmania and New Guinea, in every habitat except the driest deserts.
facts.quote: The collared sparrowhawk is widespread through mainland Australia, Tasmania and New Guinea and is found in all habitats except the driest deserts.

facts.text: DDT is thought to have reduced the thickness of its eggs by 2%, contributing to declines in cleared areas.
facts.quote: It is thought that their loss of numbers is due to the use of DDT which has reduced the thickness of collared sparrowhawks' eggs by 2%
